title: Brown Butter Chocolate-Chip Skillet Cookie + Frozen Custard
makeahead: Make dough up to 2 days ahead. Brown the butter earlier if desired.
steps: Heat oven to 350°F.
Melt butter in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking, swirling often, until the milk solids turn amber and smell nutty, 4–6 minutes. Cool 10 minutes.
Whisk brown butter with both sugars. Whisk in egg and vanilla.
Stir in flour, baking soda and salt just until combined, then fold in chocolate chips.
Press dough evenly into a lightly greased 10-inch cast-iron skillet.
Bake 18–24 minutes. The edges should be browned, but the center should still look slightly soft.
Cool 8–10 minutes so the center sets without becoming dry.
Top warm wedges—or the whole skillet—with vanilla frozen custard, hot fudge, caramel and a tiny pinch of flaky salt.
note: For the best texture, pull it earlier than feels natural. A skillet cookie continues cooking from residual heat.

title: Monster Cookie Frozen-Custard Sandwiches
ingredients: 1 pint vanilla frozen custard, slightly softened
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Line two sheet pans.
Beat peanut butter, butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in egg and vanilla.
Stir in oats, flour, baking soda and salt, then fold in chocolate chips and candy pieces.
Scoop 12 equal cookies and flatten slightly.
Bake 9–11 minutes until edges are set but centers remain soft. Cool completely.
Put a generous scoop of slightly softened frozen custard on the flat side of 6 cookies. Top with remaining cookies and press gently.
Wrap individually and freeze at least 2 hours before serving.
note: A softer cookie is important. Overbaked cookies become rock-hard once frozen.

title: Chocolate Pretzel Nachos

meta.Equipment: Sheet pan; small saucepans or microwave-safe bowls.

makeahead: Bake the chips and make sauces earlier. Assemble only when ready to eat.
ingredients: 2 cups mini pretzels or broken pretzel crisps
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Cut tortillas into triangles.
Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar. Bake 7–10 minutes, flipping once, until crisp.
Make chocolate sauce by pouring hot cream over chocolate chips; wait 2 minutes, then stir smooth.
Whisk peanut butter with powdered sugar and enough milk to make a pourable sauce.
Spread cinnamon chips and pretzels across a large platter.
Drizzle with warm chocolate, peanut-butter sauce and caramel.
Add several small scoops of frozen custard immediately before serving so everyone can scoop a little with the crunchy pieces.
note: Keep the custard in small scoops distributed around the tray instead of one giant melting mound in the middle.

title: Wisconsin Frozen Custard Mud Pie
ingredients: 1 pint chocolate frozen custard, softened 10 minutes
1 pint vanilla frozen custard, softened 10 minutes
6 chocolate sandwich cookies, roughly crushed for topping
steps: Crush 24 cookies finely and mix with melted butter.
Press firmly into a 9-inch pie plate across the bottom and up the sides. Freeze 15 minutes.
Spread chocolate frozen custard into the crust in an even layer. Freeze 20 minutes.
Warm about 1/2 cup hot fudge only until spreadable—not hot. Spread over the chocolate layer and freeze another 15 minutes.
Spread vanilla frozen custard on top. Sprinkle with crushed cookies.
Freeze at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Let stand at room temperature 8–12 minutes before slicing. Serve with remaining fudge and whipped cream if wanted.
note: Dip your knife in hot water and wipe it dry between cuts for clean slices.

title: Grasshopper Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips or finely chopped semisweet chocolate
steps: Crush cookies finely and combine with melted butter. Press into a 9-inch pie plate. Chill 20 minutes.
Combine marshmallows and milk in a saucepan over low heat. Stir constantly until the marshmallows are completely melted and the mixture is smooth. Do not boil.
Remove from heat and stir in peppermint extract and optional food coloring. Cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally so a skin does not form.
Whip 1 cup heavy cream to stiff peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the cooled mint-marshmallow mixture in three additions, keeping as much air as possible.
Fold in mini chocolate chips.
Spread into the crust and chill at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.
Before serving, whip the remaining 1/4 cup cream with powdered sugar and spoon or pipe it on top. Finish with chocolate shavings.
note: This is a classic marshmallow-and-whipped-cream style grasshopper pie — no cream cheese and no cheesecake texture. For a firmer, almost frozen slice, freeze it 2–3 hours and let it soften 10 minutes before serving.
